writeup: TIC 231908427 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 7.248248 days, identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry and pixel-level imaging. The primary eclipse produces a 2.52 percent dimming, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 46.7 in the Box Least Squares periodogram. Pixel-level difference imaging confirms a peak signal-to-noise of 10.6, though the centroid offset measures 3.0 arcseconds from the target position. No secondary eclipse was detected. The object does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, a pattern suggesting the true orbital period is twice the initial measurement. While pixel-level confirmation and eclipse timing remain consistent, this depth variation represents an open question about the system's true period and physical properties.
